intro: や joins nouns into a sample list: "A, B and things like that". The items you name are examples, and the listener understands there are others you have not mentioned. It is the open-ended partner of と, which names a complete set.

skills.rule: AやB lists nouns as examples from a larger set ("A, B and so on"); use と when the list is complete.
skills.explain:
や goes between nouns only: 机の上に本やノートがあります means there are books, notebooks and probably other things on the desk. The whole list then takes the particle its role needs, after the last item: 肉や野菜を買いました. It is often closed with など ("and so on"): りんごやみかんなど.

The real boundary is with と. AとB names exactly these things and nothing else: 父と母 is my father and my mother, full stop. AやB hints at more. So a complete set (the members of a family, the two people in a meeting) takes と, and an example list (things you bought, places you like) usually takes や.

や cannot join verbs or adjectives; for a sample list of actions use 〜たり〜たりする. や also never means "with": 友達と映画を見ました, not 友達や.
patterns: A や B [particle]  "A, B and others"
A や B や C など

examples.jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に本[ほん]{や}ノートがあります。
examples.en: There are things like books and notebooks on the desk.

examples.jp: スーパーで肉[にく]{や}野菜[やさい]を買[か]いました。
examples.en: I bought meat, vegetables and other things at the supermarket.

examples.jp: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]は公園[こうえん]{や}図書館[としょかん]に行[い]きます。
examples.en: On my days off I go to places like the park and the library.

examples.jp: りんご{や}みかんなどの果物[くだもの]が好[す]きです。
examples.en: I like fruit such as apples and mandarins.

examples.jp: 京都[きょうと]{や}奈良[なら]にはお寺[てら]がたくさんあります。
examples.en: Places like Kyoto and Nara have lots of temples.

contrast.note: AとB is a complete list: exactly A and B. AやB gives examples and implies more. と also means "with" (友達と行きます); や never does.
AもBも stresses that each named item is included (both) or excluded (neither); AやB just samples a longer list.
AかB offers a choice, "A or B": コーヒーか紅茶 is one of the two. AやB includes several items at once.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]{や}映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]{と}映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
mistakes.note: "With a friend" is と. や only lists things of the same kind.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]の家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{や}母[はは]{や}姉[あね]です。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]の家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{と}母[はは]{と}姉[あね]です。
mistakes.note: A full membership list is complete, so it takes と; や would suggest other family members you left out.

mistakes.bad: 週末[しゅうまつ]は掃除[そうじ]する{や}料理[りょうり]します。
mistakes.good: 週末[しゅうまつ]は掃除[そうじ]し{たり}料理[りょうり]し{たり}します。
mistakes.note: や joins nouns only; for a sample list of actions use 〜たり〜たりする.

skills.tip: Could you add "and so on" in English without lying? Then や. If the list is the whole set, と.
